title: Splitting the Bill
intro: A friend you had dinner with asks you to pay your share. Everyone seems to want money today.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: Can you send your share for dinner? 🍝

screen.context: You had dinner with Maya and two others last night. She paid the bill.

msg: Hey! Thanks for last night 😄 Your

msg.text: whenever, in the payment app we used last time
No hurry, and there is no link, it is just the amount.
Ask Anil, he is paying me his share too.

old.label: An old friend
old.lens: You know Maya from college, and the chat history matches.
old.why: A long history is a good sign.

share.label: A small, specific amount
share.lens: ₹850, a normal share of a dinner you really had.
share.why: It matches something you did together.

how.label: Your usual way to pay
how.lens: The same app you always use, no new account.
how.why: A familiar method is a good sign.

nolink.label: No link, no rush
nolink.lens: There is only an amount, and no hurry.
nolink.why: No link and no pressure are honest signs.

actions.label: Confirm with Maya in person or by a call, then pay her ₹850 in our usual app

go_ahead.line: You called Maya, who confirmed. You paid ₹850 in the usual app, and she thanked you.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. But a friend who paid for you is waiting for her share.

block_report.line: That was a real friend. When every message looks like a scam, real friendships get hurt too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It matched a dinner you really had, asked for a small normal amount, in the usual way, with no link and no rush. A quick call confirms it.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A small, specific request that matches something you did together, in your usual way, is likely honest. Confirm with a quick call.

quick_check.q: What made Maya's message likely honest?

options.text: It matched a dinner you really had, asked for a small amount in your usual way, with no link or rush

quick_check.explain: It matched something real, with no pressure. A quick call confirms it.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.v: Check with them in person or by call
